name: Superchunk
label: Matador
lede: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance started a band and a record label in the same Chapel Hill summer, and kept both going for more than 35 years. The band's first single was about a Kinko's co-worker; its thirteenth album came out in 2025.

eras.title: A phonebook typo, a Kinko's night shift
eras.text: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance started a band and a record label in the same Chapel Hill summer. The band's name came from a phonebook misprint, the label's from a highway sign, and the first real single was about a co-worker at the Kinko's.

years.h: A phonebook misprint names the band Chunk
years.p: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance start playing in Chapel Hill with drummer Chuck Garrison and guitarist Jack McCook. Garrison's name had been misspelled in the phonebook, and that became the band's.

years.h: A Sub Pop office tour sends them home to start Merge
years.p: Ballance and McCaughan come back from Seattle with tickets to a Mudhoney and Nirvana show and a plan to put out 7-inches by their band and friends. Ballance named the label after the merge signs she saw driving through Colorado.
years.xp:
Sub Pop had given them a tour of its office. Merge began with 7-inch singles only, packed and shipped from Ballance's bedroom, and McCaughan's contacts from his job at Schoolkids Records helped them find distributors.

In 2010 Merge put out The Suburbs by [[Arcade Fire|52074ba6-e495-4ef3-9bb4-0703888a9f68]], which went straight to No. 1 in the US and UK and won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

years.h: A New York jazz band already owns Chunk
years.p: After one single as Chunk, the band learns the name is taken. Adding Super fixes it.

years.h: The first Superchunk single is about a Kinko's co-worker
years.p: McCaughan wrote Slack Motherfucker about a slacker on his night shift at the Kinko's on Franklin Street. The first pressing on Merge is 1,000 copies and sells out fast.
years.xp:
Recorded January 18-19, 1990 at Duck Kee Studios in Raleigh, with Night Creatures on the B-side. Jack McCook painted the sleeve. College stations played it after midnight to stay clear of obscenity rules.

Drummer [[Chuck Garrison|e2cdcbfe-3f33-4acf-a168-b11979e8d72f]] has claimed the song was about him. McCaughan says it was the Kinko's guy. Ballance said "if I never hear 'Slack Motherfucker' again in my life I will be a happy camper", and the band stopped playing it for a while.

Will Hermes of WBUR wrote that it "defined the sound and the ethos of indie rock." Pitchfork ranked it No. 81 on its 1990s songs list; Spin put it 19th among the decade's singles.

years.h: The debut album goes to Matador
years.p: Matador Records, Chris Lombardi's young New York label, releases Superchunk with Slack Motherfucker on it. The reviews are strong.

years.h: Jim Wilbur replaces Jack McCook on guitar
years.p: [[Jim Wilbur|15cf0928-cc87-4d5b-bb76-e0aa68528cad]], a Connecticut-born Fairfield University graduate, takes over rhythm guitar after McCook leaves. He's still in the band.

eras.title: A new drummer, a walkout from Matador
eras.text: Two Matador albums in two years and a change of drummers. The band got faster and tighter touring with Rocket from the Crypt and Polvo, then left the label when Matador signed with Atlantic.

years.src: Wikipedia: No Pocky for Kitty · Wikipedia: Superchunk
years.h: Steve Albini records No Pocky for Kitty in three days
years.p: Superchunk cuts its second album April 21-23, 1991 at Chicago Recording Company with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]. The sleeve credits him as Laura, who sat in the right chair.
years.xp:
Pocky is a Japanese snack stick. The album runs about 33 minutes and includes Skip Steps 1 & 3, Cast Iron and Throwing Things. Garrison played drums on it but left weeks before it came out.

Merge reissued it in 1999 when Superchunk took back its Matador catalog.

years.h: Jon Wurster takes the drum stool and keeps it 31 years
years.p: Chuck Garrison quits weeks before No Pocky for Kitty comes out. [[Jon Wurster|feab5f8f-f5ac-4e63-92a8-466dde483f8c]], from the Raleigh band [[The Accelerators|abbf1897-7a1f-4e33-9a9f-612cedf550a9]], joins in October 1991.

years.h: Merge's first CD is a singles collection
years.p: Tossing Seeds (Singles 89-91), catalog MRG020, puts Slack Motherfucker in front of a much bigger audience.

years.src: Wikipedia: On the Mouth · Wikipedia: Superchunk
years.h: John Reis of Rocket from the Crypt produces On the Mouth
years.p: Recorded in a week in September 1992 at West Beach Studios with [[John Reis|626e7b64-3035-4f58-92a6-49790f600e30]], it has Wurster's first recordings with the band. Precision Auto was later covered by [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]].
years.xp:
McCaughan has said the band thought it was soaking up Rocket from the Crypt, [[Drive Like Jehu|608c9da7-d3ef-4661-828b-24bb6ae20cd6]] and Polvo from touring with them, "but, when you listen to it, it just sounds like a Superchunk record."

The song called On the Mouth isn't on On the Mouth: it's a B-side of the Mower single.

years.h: Superchunk walks when Matador signs with Atlantic
years.p: Matador's 1993 partnership with Atlantic Records is enough for the band to leave, even though it wouldn't have had to carry Atlantic's logo. Everything after this comes out on Merge.
years.xp: Matador went on to sell Capitol Records a 49 percent stake in 1996 and bought it back in 1999. Superchunk's own label kept growing: Merge became one of the biggest independent labels in America.

eras.title: Everything on Merge
eras.text: The first Merge album came after McCaughan and Ballance broke up, and the band played it every night anyway. Then came Lollapalooza, strings, a vibraphone and a tenth-birthday show for the label.

q: Touring for Foolish was so hard.
years.h: After the breakup, Foolish
years.p: Superchunk's first Merge album, recorded at Pachyderm Studios in Minnesota with Brian Paulson, comes right after Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance split as a couple. Ballance painted the cover, with herself as model.
years.xp:
Ballance said playing the songs live meant listening to the words every night and feeling mute. She still rates it her third favorite Superchunk album.

Her cover was an unpracticed homage to an [[American Music Club|5837d14e-4d18-49cf-a759-e5818714bce4]] sleeve, with a dead rabbit added after she watched Michael Moore's Pets or Meat. The Driveway to Driveway video parodies The Philadelphia Story.

years.h: A minor hit called Hyper Enough
years.p: Recorded at Fort Apache Studios in Boston, Here's Where the Strings Come In gets a video for its single. The band tours the world and plays Lollapalooza.
play: Here's Where the Strings Come In

years.h: Piano, organ and vibraphone show up on Indoor Living
years.p: After a short break and an Australian tour, Superchunk records in Bloomington, Indiana with co-producer John Plymale.
years.xp: The sessions were at Echo Park Studios in Bloomington. It was the first Superchunk record to lean on keyboards and a vibraphone.

years.h: Jim O'Rourke produces at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio
years.p: Come Pick Me Up, the seventh album, is recorded in Chicago with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] producing, and pushes further the wider sound that began on Foolish.

years.h: Merge turns ten at the Cat's Cradle
years.p: Superchunk plays the Carrboro club for the label's tenth anniversary. The set comes out in 2004 as The Clambakes Series Vol. 3.

eras.title: Pool parties and a silent film
eras.text: After Here's to Shutting Up the albums stopped for nine years, but the band never broke up. It scored a silent Japanese film, shared a 7-inch with Meatwad from Aqua Teen Hunger Force, played a Brooklyn swimming pool and Coachella, and watched Merge grow.

years.h: Eight albums in, nine quiet years start
years.p: Here's to Shutting Up is followed by occasional shows, many at the Cat's Cradle, and no new album until 2010.

years.h: Superchunk scores a 1926 silent film at the Castro Theatre
years.p: At the San Francisco International Film Festival the band plays its own score to Teinosuke Kinugasa's A Page of Madness. The recording is released as The Clambakes Series Vol. 2, 2,500 copies.

years.cap: Superchunk at the Cat's Cradle, Carrboro, North Carolina, September 1, 2006
years.h: Superchunk tops a Daily Show birthday bill at Irving Plaza
years.p: The show for The Daily Show's tenth anniversary also has Clem Snide and the show's correspondents doing stand-up. Jon Wurster drums with [[The Mountain Goats|9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef]] the same night for the first time.

years.h: A cartoon meatball gets a Superchunk B-side
years.p: A hidden track on the Aqua Teen Hunger Force movie soundtrack becomes a 7-inch: Superchunk plays Misfits and Mistakes on one side, Meatwad sings it on the other.

years.cap: Superchunk at McCarren Pool, Brooklyn, June 2007
years.h: An empty Brooklyn swimming pool hosts the first free show
years.p: Superchunk headlines the first of the McCarren Park Pool Parties.
years.xp: Around then the band also covered [[Destiny's Child|a796b92e-c137-4895-9c89-10f900617a4f]]'s Say My Name for Engine Room Recordings' Guilt by Association compilation, which came out September 4, 2007.

years.h: Coachella, eleven days after Leaves in the Gutter
years.p: Superchunk plays Indio on a bill with Yeah Yeah Yeahs and the Killers, a few days after its first new CD in seven years.
years.xp: Leaves in the Gutter came out April 7, 2009 with three unreleased tracks alongside previously released songs. Crossed Wires b/w Blinders (Fast Vers.) followed on July 7 as a 7-inch limited to 1,000 clear copies.

years.h: Our Noise puts the Merge story in a book
years.p: Mac McCaughan and Laura Ballance write the label history with John Cook. Merge turns 20 with a six-day festival across Chapel Hill and Carrboro, with more than 40 acts.

eras.title: Nine years later, still fast
eras.text: Superchunk came back after nine years sounding like it hadn't aged. Ballance left the road because of a hearing condition, a stand-in took her bass, and the band got angrier as the country did.

years.h: After nine years, Majesty Shredding
years.p: Recorded in Durham with Scott Solter, the ninth album reaches No. 85 on the Billboard 200. Rolling Stone names it one of the 30 best albums of 2010.
years.xp: The New York Times' Jon Caramanica said the band had recaptured its bright, punkish power pop with no apparent effort. [[John Darnielle|dbd4a850-1276-4aac-8d29-b43e6a186b6b]] of the Mountain Goats guests. Metacritic scored it 83.

years.h: Jeff Mangum picks Superchunk for his ATP
years.p: [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]], a Merge artist, invites the band to the All Tomorrow's Parties festival he curates in Minehead, England.

years.h: Album ten is called I Hate Music
years.p: It follows Majesty Shredding and goes on the road in North America, Australia and the UK.

years.h: Hyperacusis keeps Laura Ballance off the road
years.p: Ballance announces on the band's site that worsening hyperacusis, an extreme sensitivity to sound, rules out touring. [[Jason Narducy|82dafda1-1848-4068-b78b-487fbb4573ae]] of [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]]'s band plays bass live; she stays in the band.
years.xp: Narducy has been the touring bassist since 2013. In 2023 Betsy Wright of Ex Hex also began playing bass on the road.

years.h: Original drummer Chuck Garrison returns for one Slack Motherfucker
years.p: At the end of a Scharpling & Wurster live show in Durham, Garrison comes back to play the first single. Wurster sings it in character as Philly Boy Roy.

years.h: Four and a half years of quiet end with What a Time to Be Alive
years.p: Superchunk announced its eleventh album in November 2017.

eras.title: Director of Percussive Research, retired
eras.text: Jon Wurster left in February 2023 with a joke job title and a straight answer, and a new drummer, Laura King, played her first show a week later. In 2025 Ballance left Merge, the label she co-founded, and the band put out album thirteen.

years.h: Acoustic Foolish reworks the breakup album for Merge's 30th
years.p: Superchunk re-records its 1994 album unplugged as part of the label's 30th-anniversary releases.

years.h: Wild Loneliness is Wurster's last record with the band
years.p: The twelfth album comes out in February 2022.

years.big: "It's been a very productive thirty-one years but my heart just isn't in it anymore."
years.h: Wurster signs off on the 30th anniversary of On the Mouth
years.p: He posts on Instagram that he's fading back from his role as Director of Percussive Research at Superchunk Industries.
years.xp:
Wurster wished the band well and said he'd be around for special occasions. On the Mouth, his first album with the band, came out February 10, 1993; he announced on its 30th anniversary.

He also plays with [[The Mountain Goats|9639cd52-c351-4a17-9797-58880e95a7ef]] and [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] and co-hosts The Best Show with Tom Scharpling.

years.h: Laura King's first show is at a hockey fan fest
years.p: A week after Wurster's exit, King plays the Carolina Hurricanes' Fan Fest in Raleigh.

years.h: Secretly Group buys half of Merge, and Laura Ballance leaves
years.p: Secretly Group takes a 50% stake on June 10 and Ballance departs after 36 years. McCaughan stays on as president and head of A&R.

years.h: Songs in the Key of Yikes is Laura King's first Superchunk record
years.p: Album thirteen is the first with King on drums.
